Playbook (accumulated from past tasks):
## strategies
[ace-0002] helpful=1 harmful=0 :: Before implementing a money-related function, inspect ledgerly/money.py and existing helpers (line_total, invoice_total) to reuse to_money/ZERO/round_money and match the codebase's rounding conventions.
[ace-0004] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: When validating a quantity that must be a positive integer, reject bool explicitly (isinstance(x, bool)) before the int check, since True/False are ints in Python and would otherwise pass validation.
[ace-0005] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: Before implementing a new function, grep tests and README for the function name and expected error codes (e.g. invalid_state, invalid_quantity) to match the codebase's BillingError conventions and hidden-test expectations.
## common_mistakes
[ace-0003] helpful=1 harmful=0 :: Returning an unrounded Decimal division for a money value (e.g. weighted_total / total_quantity) fails review; wrap the final monetary result in round_money, and return ZERO for empty/zero-quantity inputs.
[ace-0006] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: Forgetting to enforce state guards (e.g. only draft invoices may be modified) on mutating functions; mirror the existing issue_invoice pattern of raising BillingError('invalid_state', ...) when status is not 'draft'.
## domain_facts
[ace-0001] helpful=1 harmful=0 :: In ledgerly, all monetary results must be rounded via ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); Python's round() and bare Decimal.quantize() use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.

item.content: When implementing date/time functions, grep for and reuse the existing ensure_utc helper (ledgerly/clock.py) to normalize inputs and mirror sibling modules (e.g. subscriptions.current_period) for period arithmetic conventions.

Computing 'first renewal strictly after X' with a plain floor division can return the start itself or a non-strict result; use n = (after - start) // length + 1 and handle after < start explicitly to guarantee strictness.

In ledgerly, datetimes must be timezone-aware; ensure_utc raises BillingError('naive_datetime') for naive inputs and BillingError('invalid_datetime') for non-datetimes, so normalize all datetime arguments before arithmetic.
